findings.claim: The digest treats a memory as a workflow mirror, and collapses it into the single 'mirrors' line, when its type is 'architecture' and its topic_key starts with 'sdd/', 'odd/' or 'project/'. It does not check that the memory is an automated mirror. A hand-saved architecture memory under a 'project/...' topic key is therefore hidden from the session-start digest. Only the newest such memory shows, with '(+N more mirrors)', and the older ones can be found only through mem_search. The test pins 'project/app/manifest/context' as a mirror but never covers a real architecture note under 'project/'. I did not run this. I read the code, and the test shows 'project/app/demo-first' is kept only because its type is 'decision'.

DigestText returns an error, and no digest text, when the appended search fails after the digest was built successfully. Both 'memorycard context --query' and mem_context with a query then fail completely and discard a valid digest. A failure of the optional hits section should degrade to the digest alone, perhaps with a note. I did not find a concrete trigger, because ftsQuery sanitizes the query and the tests show a lexical fallback when the embedder is unavailable. This is a graceful-degradation concern only.

After this change 'memorycard context' parses flags. An unknown flag exits 2, and any positional word becomes a search query. A caller that passes extra arguments, or a query beginning with '-', now gets exit 2 or an extra 'top hits' section, where before it printed the plain digest. This behaviour change was declared in the Risk line. The grep found no in-repo caller that passes arguments to 'context', so the impact is limited to external hooks. The new test covers the --bogus case.
